content: Psyllium is a bulk-forming laxative that is prescribed to treat constipation. It works by absorbing liquid in the intestines, swelling, and forming a bulky stool that is easier to pass. In some cases, psyllium may be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about its use, consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Psyllium is available in various forms, including powder, granules, and wafers, and is taken orally. It is typically taken one to three times daily. Follow the instructions on the package or prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take psyllium exactly as directed. Do not take more or less than prescribed or take it more frequently than instructed by your doctor. The powder and granules must be mixed with 8 ounces of a pleasant-tasting liquid, such as fruit juice, immediately before use. Wafers should be chewed thoroughly. To ensure psyllium works effectively and to prevent side effects, drink at least 8 ounces of liquid when taking it. Do not use psyllium for longer than one week unless directed by your doctor. In addition to treating constipation, psyllium may also be prescribed to manage diarrhea or high cholesterol. Discuss the potential risks of using this medication for your specific condition with your doctor. Before taking psyllium, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to psyllium or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including vitamins. Avoid taking digoxin (Lanoxin), salicylates (aspirin), or nitrofurantoin (Macrodantin, Furadantin, Macrobid) within three hours of taking psyllium. Let your doctor know if you have or have ever had diabetes mellitus, heart disease, high blood pressure, kidney disease, rectal bleeding, intestinal blockage, or difficulty swallowing. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking psyllium, contact your doctor immediately. Additionally, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are on a low-sugar or low-sodium diet. Be cautious not to inhale psyllium powder when preparing a dose, as accidental inhalation can cause allergic reactions. If you miss a scheduled dose of psyllium, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Psyllium may cause side effects. If you experience any of the following symptoms, contact your doctor immediately: difficulty breathing, stomach pain, difficulty swallowing, skin rash, itching, upset stomach, or vomiting. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store psyllium in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist about the correct disposal method. If you have any questions about taking psyllium, ask your doctor or pharmacist for clarification.
